1vfn5yn.q: Grip force allows the vehicle to move.
1vfn5yn.why: Grip force (forza aderente) is the friction between tyre and road. Without it a vehicle cannot accelerate, brake or move.

7lfpk9.q: Grip force opposes sliding toward the outside of a bend.
7lfpk9.why: In a bend, grip force counters the centrifugal force pushing the vehicle outward and prevents it from sliding.

13b3m3y.q: Grip force allows the vehicle to follow the intended path.
13b3m3y.why: Thanks to grip force the wheels transmit steering input to the road, so the vehicle follows the path the driver intends.

1v5015k.q: Grip force opposes the tyre sliding on the asphalt.
1v5015k.why: Grip is exactly the force that holds the tyre on the asphalt and resists its sliding.

y63kbg.q: Grip force does not oppose sliding caused by crosswind.
y63kbg.why: Grip force resists any sideways slide, including one caused by crosswind or centrifugal force.

juf867.q: Excessive grip force causes the brakes to overheat.
juf867.why: Brake overheating comes from excessive or prolonged braking, not from grip force.

kyu00i.q: Grip force increases if the asphalt is rough.
kyu00i.why: Rough asphalt gives the tyres more friction, so grip force increases.

1i7h9ee.q: Grip force decreases if the asphalt is wet.
1i7h9ee.why: Water between tyre and asphalt reduces friction, so grip decreases.

7te1yf.q: Grip force increases if the asphalt is wet.
7te1yf.why: On wet asphalt grip decreases, not increases. It is greatest on a dry, clean road.

za58gu.q: Grip force increases if the asphalt is covered with leaves.
za58gu.why: Leaves make the surface slippery and reduce grip, especially when wet.

y5mb7z.q: Grip force increases if the asphalt is covered with ice.
y5mb7z.why: Ice sharply reduces friction, so grip drops considerably rather than rising.

1h5z8e7.q: Grip force increases if the asphalt is covered with mud.
1h5z8e7.why: Mud between tyre and road reduces grip rather than increasing it.

1c9gj3f.q: If the coefficient of grip decreases, the driving wheels may spin.
1c9gj3f.why: With less grip the driving wheels cannot transfer power to the road and may spin.

1qubm2d.q: If the coefficient of grip decreases, the braking distance increases.
1qubm2d.why: Less grip means less available braking force, so the braking distance gets longer.

14c0w4f.q: If the coefficient of grip is low, speed must be reduced.
14c0w4f.why: With low grip, braking distances grow and control drops, so you must reduce speed.

1osksyu.q: If the coefficient of grip decreases, the braking distance gets shorter.
1osksyu.why: When grip decreases the braking distance increases; it does not get shorter.

8ckfjy.q: If the coefficient of grip is low, speed must be reduced only in bends.
8ckfjy.why: With low grip you must reduce speed everywhere, including on straight roads, because braking distances increase.

12ae1w0.q: A low coefficient of grip limits the speed at which a bend can be taken safely.
12ae1w0.why: With low grip, centrifugal force soon exceeds grip, so the safe speed in a bend is lower.

yr90nb.q: A low coefficient of grip makes skidding in bends more likely.
yr90nb.why: When grip is low, centrifugal force overcomes friction more easily and the vehicle skids in bends.

sey4tn.q: A low coefficient of grip increases the braking distance.
sey4tn.why: Less grip reduces usable braking force and so lengthens the braking distance.

159yei3.q: A low coefficient of grip makes sudden braking dangerous.
159yei3.why: With low grip, hard braking can lock the wheels and cause loss of control.

7d64wq.q: A low coefficient of grip does not affect the vehicle's speed.
7d64wq.why: Low grip forces you to reduce speed, so it clearly does affect it.

b50kz2.q: A low coefficient of grip reduces the braking distance.
b50kz2.why: With low grip the braking distance increases, not decreases.

9i1dqp.q: A low coefficient of grip reduces fuel consumption.
9i1dqp.why: Grip does not lower fuel use. Low grip makes wheels slip, which wastes efficiency.

7pqfpp.q: A low coefficient of grip reduces skidding in bends.
7pqfpp.why: Low grip makes skidding in bends more likely, not less.

1vo90ww.q: A motorcyclist must bear in mind that grip decreases on rails, especially in the rain.
1vo90ww.why: Rails, especially when wet, are very slippery for a motorcycle's narrow tyres.

16jojbk.q: A motorcyclist must bear in mind that grip decreases on road marking stripes when it rains.
16jojbk.why: Wet road marking stripes (segnaletica orizzontale) are slippery and reduce a motorcycle's grip.

1fwtw2m.q: A motorcyclist must bear in mind that grip does not depend on the type of road surface.
1fwtw2m.why: Grip depends heavily on the road surface: asphalt, cobbles, gravel or a wet road all give different friction.

1acyrd8.q: A motorcyclist must bear in mind that grip decreases when carrying a passenger.
1acyrd8.why: Grip depends on the road and the tyres. A passenger changes the bike's handling, not the grip coefficient.

19st30j.q: Grip force decreases if the road is dirty with oil.
19st30j.why: Oil on the asphalt forms a slippery film that greatly reduces friction and therefore grip.

11ti7fz.q: Grip force is greater if the asphalt is dry and clean.
11ti7fz.why: On dry, clean asphalt the friction between tyre and road is at its maximum.

64yzlu.q: Grip force does not depend on tyre pressure.
64yzlu.why: Wrong pressure distorts the tyre's contact patch and reduces grip, so grip does depend on it.

9p7wfz.q: When a vehicle goes round a bend, a force acts on it that tends to push it outward.
9p7wfz.why: In a bend, centrifugal force acts on the vehicle and tends to push it toward the outside.

1i820j5.q: When a vehicle goes round a bend, excessive speed can cause it to skid.
1i820j5.why: At excessive speed, centrifugal force exceeds grip and the vehicle skids.

1gproi9.q: When a vehicle goes round a bend, excessive speed can cause it to roll over.
1gproi9.why: At excessive speed, centrifugal force can roll the vehicle over, especially a tall or loaded one.

1hdrqxe.q: When a vehicle goes round a bend, a force acts on it that tends to push it inward.
1hdrqxe.why: In a bend centrifugal force pushes the vehicle outward, not inward.

f27npi.q: When going round a bend you must increase speed to avoid skidding.
f27npi.why: Speeding up increases centrifugal force and promotes skidding. You must slow down in a bend.

mfhq70.q: When going round a bend you must increase speed to avoid rolling over.
mfhq70.why: More speed means more overturning force. To avoid a rollover you must slow down.

jdhoye.q: Rolling over in a bend is made more likely by a high load.
jdhoye.why: A high load raises the centre of gravity, making the vehicle less stable and likelier to roll over.

1h6qbvd.q: Rolling over in a bend is made more likely by a load that is not firmly secured.
1h6qbvd.why: A badly secured load can shift in a bend, upset the balance and make a rollover more likely.

piu91y.q: Rolling over in a bend is made more likely by a short distance between wheels on the same axle (narrow track).
piu91y.why: A narrow track reduces sideways stability and makes rollover more likely.

5avbpn.q: Rolling over in a bend is made more likely by a small bend radius (tight bend).
5avbpn.why: In a tight bend centrifugal force is greater, so the rollover risk rises.

1vwpz0h.q: Rolling over in a bend is made more likely by a wide distance between wheels on the same axle (wide track).
1vwpz0h.why: A wide track increases stability and reduces the risk of rolling over.

1790mye.q: Rolling over in a bend is made more likely by a low load.
1790mye.why: A low load lowers the centre of gravity and makes the vehicle more stable, reducing rollover risk.

1evdb6w.q: Rolling over in a bend is made more likely by a large bend radius (wide bend).
1evdb6w.why: In a wide bend centrifugal force is smaller, so the rollover risk is lower.

10v7i1m.q: The overturning force in a bend increases as speed increases.
10v7i1m.why: Centrifugal force grows with the square of speed, so the overturning force rises as well.

m4pqxb.q: The overturning force in a bend decreases as speed increases.
m4pqxb.why: As speed increases the overturning force increases, not decreases.

dh0dz8.q: ABS prevents the wheels from locking.
dh0dz8.why: ABS (anti-lock braking system) modulates brake pressure and stops the wheels from locking when braking.

1pv921j.q: ABS makes it possible to correct the vehicle's path even during emergency braking.
1pv921j.why: Because the wheels do not lock, ABS lets you steer and correct your path even in emergency braking.

urvwla.q: ABS makes it possible to use maximum grip force when braking.
urvwla.why: ABS keeps the wheels at the limit of grip without locking them, using the maximum grip available when braking.

1la0jju.q: ABS can act on all wheels, intervening in turn on those about to lock up during braking.
1la0jju.why: ABS monitors all wheels and steps in on whichever one is about to lock.

1j87e6f.q: ABS also works when the tyres are worn.
1j87e6f.why: ABS still works with worn tyres, although wear reduces grip and lengthens braking.

x8x8rt.q: ABS also works when the asphalt is wet.
x8x8rt.why: ABS works on any surface, including wet asphalt, where the risk of wheel lock is higher.

1ti4ch0.q: ABS makes braking safer because it prevents the wheels from locking.
1ti4ch0.why: By preventing wheel lock, ABS preserves steering and stability, making braking safer.

1ppwjad.why: ABS exists precisely to prevent the wheels from locking when braking.

ot9ja4.q: ABS prevents the vehicle's path from being changed during braking.
ot9ja4.why: With ABS the wheels do not lock, so you can steer and change path even while braking.

zv12ei.q: ABS prevents the use of maximum grip force when braking.
zv12ei.why: ABS allows the maximum available grip to be used; it does not prevent it.

td07vf.q: ABS does not act on the driven wheels.
td07vf.why: ABS acts on all wheels, including the driven ones (ruote motrici).

j2oug.q: ABS does not activate if the tyres are worn.
j2oug.why: ABS activates even with worn tyres whenever the wheels are about to lock.

21mde3.q: The tyre inflation pressure must be checked regularly, including that of the spare wheel.
21mde3.why: Pressure must be checked regularly on every tyre, including the spare wheel (ruota di scorta), so it is ready when needed.

ilmrkf.q: Tyre inflation pressure must be adjusted to the vehicle's weight conditions.
ilmrkf.why: The correct pressure depends on the vehicle's load, so it must be adjusted to the weight carried.

ylmc62.q: The correct tyre inflation pressure depends on the vehicle's load and the number of passengers carried.
ylmc62.why: The manufacturer specifies different pressures depending on the load and the number of passengers.

1bjmcxt.q: Insufficient tyre inflation pressure increases friction and also fuel consumption.
1bjmcxt.why: An underinflated tyre flexes more, which raises rolling friction and therefore fuel consumption.

9328v.q: Tyre inflation pressure must be checked when the tyre is cold.
9328v.why: Heat from driving raises the pressure, so a correct reading is taken with the tyre cold.

pwdzc.q: The automatic tyre pressure monitoring system increases the safety of vehicles fitted with it.
pwdzc.why: The automatic monitoring system (TPMS) warns of pressure loss straight away, which increases safety.

1b2tkzm.q: If tyre inflation pressure is measured when the tyre is hot, the pressure reading is correct.
1b2tkzm.why: A hot tyre reads higher than its true pressure, so the reading is misleading. Measure it cold.

slhh40.q: Tyre inflation pressure must be checked after driving a few kilometres, as soon as the tyre has heated up.
slhh40.why: The check must be done with a cold tyre. After a few kilometres the heat distorts the reading.

19aj5bo.q: Tyre inflation pressure must be set according to the material of the rims (steel, alloy, etc.).
19aj5bo.why: Pressure depends on the load and the manufacturer's specification, not on the rim material.

1kamq77.q: Before starting a long journey, it is advisable to increase the tyre inflation pressure.
1kamq77.why: Pressure should be set to the manufacturer's value for the actual load, not raised arbitrarily.

spuw5.q: On vehicles with a trailer, the tyre inflation pressure of the towing vehicle must be the same as that of the trailer.
spuw5.why: Each vehicle has its own pressure based on its manufacturer and load, so the towing vehicle and trailer can differ.

1sbv1wr.q: The minimum tread depth of a motor vehicle's tyres must be 1.6 millimetres.
1sbv1wr.why: For motor vehicles (autoveicoli) the minimum tread depth (battistrada) is 1.6 mm.

wq6j3p.q: It is advisable to replace tyres after a few years, even if they are not worn.
wq6j3p.why: Rubber hardens and ages over time, losing grip and reliability even when the tread still looks good, so replacing tyres after some years is recommended.

fu2uko.q: The minimum tread depth of a motorcycle's tyres must be 1.0 millimetres.
fu2uko.why: Motorcycle tyres need at least 1.0 mm of tread (battistrada); cars need 1.6 mm.

1slc4xv.q: If a nail has become lodged in a "tubeless" tyre, you can, with due care, keep driving, stopping as soon as possible to repair the damage.
1slc4xv.why: A tubeless tyre usually keeps its air around a nail stuck in it, so you can continue carefully and stop as soon as possible to have it repaired.

qoha1f.why: With no inner tube, a punctured tubeless tyre loses pressure slowly, giving you time to stop safely.

l88unf.q: "Tubeless" tyres can only be repaired with special spray cans containing a special sealant that closes the hole from the inside.
l88unf.why: Sealant cans are only an emergency fix; a tubeless tyre can also be properly repaired with plugs or patches by a tyre specialist (gommista).

r2z2hp.q: Tyres with an inner tube deflate slowly when punctured.
r2z2hp.why: With an inner tube, a puncture usually causes fast deflation, which can make you lose control of the vehicle.

1t8d2kb.q: If a nail has become lodged in a "tubeless" tyre, it must be removed immediately to prevent the tyre from exploding.
1t8d2kb.why: Pulling the nail out would let the air escape at once, so it should stay in until repair. The tyre does not explode.

1ug96yb.q: Tyres inflated with nitrogen must be kept at a lower pressure than those with compressed air.
1ug96yb.why: The correct pressure is the one given by the vehicle manufacturer, whatever gas is used for inflation.

1pdyt5n.q: Studded tyres may be used only during a predetermined period of the year.
1pdyt5n.why: Studded tyres (pneumatici chiodati) are allowed only in a set winter period, generally 15 November to 15 March.

1y6kvc6.q: It is advisable to fit winter tyres on all wheels.
1y6kvc6.why: Winter tyres on all wheels keep the vehicle's behaviour uniform, with balanced grip and stability.

guudc1.q: Anyone using snow chains that are not type-approved is liable to a penalty as if they had none.
guudc1.why: Snow chains must be type-approved (omologate); non-approved ones count as having no chains and are fined.

7bjpyn.q: Studded tyres must be fitted only on two wheels of the same axle.
7bjpyn.why: Studded tyres must be fitted on all of the vehicle's wheels, not just on one axle.

9upj9s.q: In dual-drive vehicles (so-called 4x4), snow chains must be fitted on the rear wheels.
9upj9s.why: Chains go on the driving wheels; on a 4x4 you follow the manufacturer's handbook, so they are not always on the rear wheels.

f5zi4n.q: The suspension components are not damaged if tyres with chains are used on stretches of road free of snow.
f5zi4n.why: On snow-free road, chains put heavy stress on suspension and transmission parts and can damage them, so they should be removed.

ugbwy6.q: Vehicles fitted with winter tyres must observe lower maximum speed limits than ordinary ones.
ugbwy6.why: The usual speed limits apply. A limit arises only if the winter tyres' speed rating is below the vehicle's top speed.

11tmgf7.q: To change a wheel, it is best to park the vehicle on level, stable ground.
11tmgf7.why: On level, firm ground the vehicle cannot roll and the jack (cric) will not slip, so the job is safe.

zat78j.q: Before changing a wheel, you must apply the parking brake and engage first gear or reverse.
zat78j.why: Parking brake and a gear engaged stop the vehicle from moving while it is raised.

10b44nr.q: Before lifting the vehicle to change a wheel, it is advisable to slightly loosen the fixing bolts.
10b44nr.why: While the wheel is still on the ground it cannot spin, so the bolts can be loosened more easily.

108cohz.q: When changing a wheel using the jack (cric), you must avoid getting under the vehicle.
108cohz.why: The jack can fail or slip, so getting under a raised vehicle risks being crushed.

fvt3bh.q: To change a wheel, after raising the vehicle and fitting the spare wheel, you must tighten the bolts lightly while the vehicle is raised and complete the tightening only after lowering it.
fvt3bh.why: A raised wheel spins, so the bolts are only snugged up first and fully tightened once the wheel is back on the ground.

12vqwld.q: In case of a puncture, before changing the wheel, it is advisable to have all passengers get out of the vehicle and stand, for safety, off the carriageway.
12vqwld.why: Passengers standing off the carriageway (carreggiata), for example behind the guardrail, are protected from traffic during the change.

9m0koq.q: To remove a wheel that needs replacing, you must remove the bolts before lifting the vehicle with the jack (cric).
9m0koq.why: Bolts are only loosened with the wheel on the ground; the vehicle is then lifted and they are fully removed.

q5658h.q: To remove a wheel, you must position the jack (cric) at any point of the vehicle's side member.
q5658h.why: The jack must go only at the lifting points specified by the manufacturer, not at just any point.

188melw.q: To remove a wheel, you must position the jack (cric) as far as possible from the wheel to be replaced.
188melw.why: The jack goes at the designated lifting point, as close as possible to the wheel being changed.

j0gav1.q: Fitting the "ruotino" (small-size spare wheel) allows a speed of 120 km/h to be reached.
j0gav1.why: With a space-saver spare (ruotino) the maximum speed is 80 km/h, driving carefully until it is replaced.

ms7j73.q: In vehicles with the "ruotino" fitted (small-size spare wheel), carrying passengers is not permitted.
ms7j73.why: The ruotino only imposes a speed limit of 80 km/h; carrying passengers is still allowed.

98gow0.q: In emergency braking with the ABS activating, you must keep pressing the pedal hard, without easing the pressure.
98gow0.why: ABS prevents wheel lock by modulating braking, so keep the pedal firmly pressed to benefit from it.

1cyoz12.q: The braking action exerted by the engine is greatest if first gear is engaged.
1cyoz12.why: Engine braking increases with lower gears, so it is greatest in first gear.

9nug8t.q: Prolonged and repeated use of the brakes, causing them to overheat, reduces braking efficiency.
9nug8t.why: Overheated brakes lose effectiveness (fading), lengthening braking distances.

1ebmetx.q: When driving down long, steep descents, you must engage a low gear to avoid overheating the brakes.
1ebmetx.why: A low gear uses engine braking and relieves the brakes, so they do not overheat.

sl4v74.q: After washing the vehicle, it is advisable to carry out a braking test.
sl4v74.why: Water on discs and pads temporarily reduces braking; a brief test brake dries them and checks they work.

1rgldsj.q: In emergency braking with the ABS activating, you must immediately reduce the pressure on the brake pedal.
1rgldsj.why: With ABS you must not ease off; keep the pedal pressed hard and the system prevents wheel lock.

136b55m.q: All vehicles are fitted with a parking brake operated by a manual control.
136b55m.why: The parking brake may be hand-operated, foot-operated or electric, so not all are manual.

52l7lj.q: The parking brake is used while driving, to brake or stop the vehicle.
52l7lj.why: The parking brake holds a parked vehicle; while driving you use the service brake, apart from emergencies.

if71w1.q: When driving down long, steep descents, it is advisable to drive with the gearbox in neutral to save fuel and brakes.
if71w1.why: In neutral there is no engine braking and the brakes overheat, so descend with a gear engaged.

1mp4xb9.q: After an accident, if there is a risk of the vehicle catching fire, it is advisable to switch off the electrical system by turning the ignition key.
1mp4xb9.why: Switching off the ignition removes a possible source of sparks and stops the fuel pump.

gexal1.q: If a vehicle starts to catch fire and there is no extinguisher, sand or earth can be thrown at the base of the flames.
gexal1.why: Sand or earth smothers flames by cutting off oxygen, and should be thrown at the base of the fire.

kmufhk.q: After an accident, if the vehicle starts to catch fire and there is no extinguisher, a wet blanket can be used to put out the flames.
kmufhk.why: A wet blanket smothers flames and can be used when no extinguisher is available.

m9bjfx.q: After an accident, if the vehicle starts to catch fire, its fuel tank must be emptied immediately.
m9bjfx.why: Emptying the tank is dangerous and not useful; fight the fire with an extinguisher or similar and move away.

4cc6y4.q: After an accident, the risk of fire is greater if the vehicle has an inertia switch that cuts the fuel supply to the engine.
4cc6y4.why: An inertia switch cuts off the fuel pump after an impact, which lowers the fire risk.

16h4bou.q: After an accident, if a vehicle running on LPG starts to catch fire, the tank containing the fuel must be removed immediately.
16h4bou.why: Removing an LPG tank in an emergency is dangerous and impractical; move away and call the emergency services.

13ywxkn.q: It is inadvisable to place objects under the driver's seat, as they might slide during driving and get in the way of the driver's movements.
13ywxkn.why: Objects under the seat can slide and jam the pedals, compromising control of the vehicle.

rudh5f.q: Using a mobile phone without a "hands-free" kit or earpiece is prohibited while driving.
rudh5f.why: While driving you may use a phone only with hands-free or an earpiece, which keep both hands free.

umy0y3.q: When carrying children, it is advisable to engage the safety device that prevents the doors from being opened from inside the vehicle.
umy0y3.why: The child lock (blocco di sicurezza) stops a child from opening the door while the vehicle is moving.

1jejeyw.q: The air conditioner can usefully be used in winter too, to quickly demist the windscreen.
1jejeyw.why: Air conditioning dries the air and clears the windscreen quickly, even in winter.

1875ylu.q: While driving, it is permitted to use a mobile phone to type text messages.
1875ylu.why: Texting while driving is prohibited because it takes your attention and hands away from driving.

ofk1ld.q: Satellite navigation systems fitted to some vehicles must be programmed while the vehicle is moving.
ofk1ld.why: Set the satnav while stopped; doing it while moving distracts you from driving.

bobdwj.q: Variable message panels give danger indications but cannot have prescriptive value (obligation, prohibition).
bobdwj.why: Variable message panels can also give mandatory instructions, such as obligations and prohibitions, besides danger warnings.

1p0s5uh.q: When the road is wet, if the vehicle ahead throws up water that dirties my windscreen, I must overtake it immediately.
1p0s5uh.why: Overtaking at once is dangerous; increase your following distance so less spray reaches your windscreen.

36xcmn.q: Stickers, pendants or other objects applied to the vehicle's windows can reduce the driver's visibility.
36xcmn.why: Stickers and objects on the glass restrict the field of view and can hide obstacles or other road users.

72ngdu.q: Clean, transparent vehicle windows ensure better outside visibility.
72ngdu.why: Clean, clear glass gives the best view of the outside.

1qet409.q: The windscreen wiper blades must be checked and replaced if they are worn.
1qet409.why: Worn blades clear the glass poorly and reduce visibility in rain, so they must be replaced.

opled6.q: You must check that the windscreen washer reservoir always contains liquid for cleaning the windows.
opled6.why: Washer fluid cleans the windscreen, so its level should always be checked and topped up.

12kxo7w.q: In case of damage or breakage of the vehicle's front glass, it must be repaired with transparent adhesive tape.
12kxo7w.why: Adhesive tape is not a valid repair; a damaged windscreen must be repaired or replaced by a workshop.

1ny22v3.q: If the windscreen is covered in dust, the demisting device must be used.
1ny22v3.why: Demisting works against condensation; dust is removed with the washer and wipers.

ublio9.q: For greater safety, you must use exclusively tyres of the sizes provided for by the vehicle's type approval.
ublio9.why: Only the tyre sizes specified in the vehicle's approval and registration document should be used, for safety and road holding.

2w1cqz.q: For greater safety, identical tyres must be used on the wheels of the same axle.
2w1cqz.why: Identical tyres on the same axle give even grip and braking, avoiding swerving.

14t8sbq.q: For greater safety, you must check the condition of the tyres on the sides as well, to prevent sudden bursts or deflation.
14t8sbq.why: The sidewalls (fianchi) can have cuts or bulges that cause sudden bursts or deflation, so they should be checked.

sps29h.q: To guarantee the vehicle's grip and stability, you must check that the tyre inflation pressure is the one recommended by the manufacturer.
sps29h.why: The correct pressure, given by the manufacturer, ensures grip, stability and even wear.

j77s8p.q: Too low a tyre inflation pressure causes abnormal wear at the edges.
j77s8p.why: With low pressure the tyre rests on its shoulders, so the edges wear faster than the centre.

1p3j8c3.q: You must never swap the position of the tyres, so that they can adapt better.
1p3j8c3.why: Rotating tyres periodically is recommended to even out their wear.

hng01e.q: To guarantee the vehicle's grip and stability, you only need to check the inflation pressure of the drive wheels' tyres.
hng01e.why: Pressure must be checked on all wheels, including the spare.

10z4a8q.q: To improve tyre cooling, the inflation pressure must be reduced.
10z4a8q.why: Low pressure makes the tyre flex more and overheat; use the pressure prescribed by the manufacturer.

1rm5tto.q: Too low a tyre inflation pressure causes abnormal wear of both the central part and the edges.
1rm5tto.why: Too low pressure wears the edges; it is overinflation that wears the centre.

1430zfx.q: The braking systems of light vehicles are often fitted with a brake servo.
1430zfx.why: A brake servo boosts the force applied to the pedal and is common on light vehicles.

2xnnkk.q: In braking systems, the vehicle's kinetic energy is converted into heat by friction.
2xnnkk.why: In braking, friction between pads or linings and discs or drums turns kinetic energy into heat.

1vxa8uq.q: The parts of the braking system most stressed by high temperatures are the friction linings.
1vxa8uq.why: The friction linings (pastiglie and ganasce) take the most heat and lose effectiveness when overheated.

iwnjf7.q: The parking brake must be used to hold a parked vehicle or in emergency situations.
iwnjf7.why: The parking brake holds a parked vehicle and can serve as an emergency brake.

1i9tjap.q: The level of the hydraulic brake fluid must be checked periodically.
1i9tjap.why: A low brake fluid level indicates a leak or wear and compromises braking, so check it regularly.

fbi1yx.q: The parking brake must be able to keep the parked vehicle locked even on sloping roads.
fbi1yx.why: The parking brake must hold the vehicle even on a slope.

ykwzkz.q: The vacuum brake servo cannot work with the engine off.
ykwzkz.why: The vacuum servo relies on engine vacuum; with the engine off the pedal gets hard and needs much more force.

lfxz0b.q: The parking brake must not be used for service braking.
lfxz0b.why: The parking brake (freno di stazionamento) only holds a stationary vehicle. To slow down while driving you use the service brake, operated by the pedal.

1ih45mj.q: The braking circuit of light vehicles is a sealed circuit, so periodic checking of the hydraulic fluid level is not necessary.
1ih45mj.why: Brake fluid must be checked regularly and replaced on schedule. The level can drop through pad wear or leaks, and the fluid degrades with age, so the circuit is not maintenance-free.

1ti8pbk.q: The parking brake must be used for service braking when driving on steep roads, in order to reduce overheating of the braking components.
1ti8pbk.why: The parking brake is never a service brake. On long descents use engine braking (freno motore) in a low gear and keep pedal use to a minimum.

1xw6jtp.q: The vacuum brake servo can also work with the engine off, as long as the ignition key is in the switch.
1xw6jtp.why: The vacuum brake servo (servofreno) relies on vacuum produced by the running engine. With the engine off its assistance runs out and the pedal becomes very hard, whether or not the key is in.

1oofwao.q: In an emergency braking situation, the driver must quickly engage reverse gear.
1oofwao.why: In emergency braking you press the brake pedal firmly. Engaging reverse while moving would damage the gearbox and would not help stop the vehicle.

2f39mv.q: Poor or unbalanced braking can be caused by air or vapour in the hydraulic braking circuit.
2f39mv.why: Air or vapour in the hydraulic circuit is compressible, so it reduces the pressure reaching the brakes and makes braking weak or uneven.

c5ewco.q: Poor or unbalanced braking can be caused by excessive wear of the brake linings.
c5ewco.why: Heavily worn brake linings (guarnizioni frenanti) give less friction, and uneven wear between wheels makes braking weak or unbalanced.

1mkzwwx.q: Poor or unbalanced braking can be caused by uneven wear of the drums or discs.
1mkzwwx.why: Drums or discs worn unevenly reduce the contact area with the linings, so braking becomes weak or unbalanced.

kygq44.q: Poor or unbalanced braking can be caused by different tyre pressures on the same axle.
kygq44.why: Different pressures on the same axle give different grip, so one wheel brakes more than the other and braking is unbalanced.

1efdnzf.q: Poor braking can be caused by excessive heating of the brake linings.
1efdnzf.why: Overheated linings lose friction (known as fading), so braking becomes less effective and stopping distance increases.

koinrg.q: Poor or unbalanced braking can be caused by an excessive or badly distributed load.
koinrg.why: An excessive or badly distributed load changes the weight on the wheels and their grip, making braking less effective or unbalanced.

vhfe58.q: Poor braking can be caused by excessive and repeated braking.
vhfe58.why: Repeated, prolonged braking overheats the brakes and linings, which then lose effectiveness. On descents use engine braking instead.

rww5f1.q: With unbalanced brakes, it can happen that only the wheels on one side lock up when braking.
rww5f1.why: With unbalanced brakes, the wheels on one side may brake much harder than the other side and lock up first.

16ojpb.q: With unbalanced brakes, it can happen that when braking the vehicle skids, heading towards the side of the wheel that locks first.
16ojpb.why: Unbalanced brakes pull harder on one side, so the vehicle swerves towards the side of the wheel that locks first.

x0hlt6.q: With unbalanced brakes, irregular and uneven tyre tread wear is generally seen.
x0hlt6.why: Unbalanced brakes make the wheels work unequally, which usually causes irregular, uneven tread (battistrada) wear.

z6jem5.q: Poor or unbalanced braking can be caused by excessive wear of the parking brake mechanisms.
z6jem5.why: The parking brake has its own mechanism, separate from the service braking system, so its wear does not affect braking while driving.

ov9u26.q: Poor or unbalanced braking can be caused by insufficient lubrication of the drums or discs.
ov9u26.why: Drums and discs must not be lubricated because braking depends on friction. Grease or oil on them actually reduces braking efficiency.

d6vyw.q: Poor or unbalanced braking can be caused by excessive play in the clutch pedal.
d6vyw.why: The clutch pedal belongs to the transmission, not the braking system, so its play does not affect braking.

1ir5642.q: Poor or unbalanced braking can be caused by the presence of power steering on small-engine vehicles.
1ir5642.why: Power steering (servosterzo) only eases turning the wheel and is not part of the braking system, so it does not impair braking.

1o45glw.q: Poor or unbalanced braking can be caused by the presence of disc brakes on the rear axle.
1o45glw.why: Rear disc brakes are a normal design and, if in good condition, do not cause poor or unbalanced braking.

lzbp2u.q: Poor or unbalanced braking can be caused by winter tyres fitted on all four wheels.
lzbp2u.why: Four matching winter tyres give uniform behaviour across all wheels, so they do not cause unbalanced braking.

pjnr8m.q: Poor or unbalanced braking can be caused by winter tyres used on roads without snow.
pjnr8m.why: Winter tyres may be used on snow-free roads too. Fitted correctly on all four wheels they do not cause unbalanced braking.

10tuk7f.q: Poor or unbalanced braking can be caused by using methane-fuelled vehicles on mountain roads.
10tuk7f.why: Methane fuel has no effect on brake efficiency. On mountain roads what matters is using engine braking correctly.

130gnea.q: With unbalanced brakes, overheating of the engine coolant is generally seen.
130gnea.why: Engine coolant belongs to the cooling system, not the brakes, so unbalanced brakes do not overheat it.

1pbpvdr.q: On very steep descents it is good to drive with the handbrake partially engaged.
1pbpvdr.why: The handbrake must not be used while driving: it overheats and can lock the rear wheels. On descents use a low gear (engine braking).

tbnzno.q: Replacing the brake pads is routine maintenance that any driver can carry out.
tbnzno.why: Changing brake pads affects the braking system and therefore safety, so it must be done by qualified mechanics in a workshop.

uov9z0.q: The suspension of a motor vehicle is located between the chassis and the wheels.
uov9z0.why: The suspension (sospensioni) connects the chassis to the wheels, absorbing road irregularities.

77k56h.q: The suspension of a motor vehicle serves to ensure good ride comfort.
77k56h.why: The suspension absorbs bumps and vibrations from the road surface, giving a comfortable ride.

kcxp6q.q: The suspension of a motor vehicle serves to ensure that the wheels stay in contact with the road surface.
kcxp6q.why: The suspension keeps the wheels in contact with the road even over bumps, ensuring grip and road holding.

6mex1w.q: The suspension of a motor vehicle serves to dampen the shocks transmitted by uneven ground.
6mex1w.why: One job of the suspension is to dampen shocks from uneven ground so they do not reach the chassis.

offb42.q: The suspension of a motor vehicle helps make driving more comfortable and safer.
offb42.why: The suspension improves both comfort and safety by keeping the wheels gripping and softening shocks.

1g7rlqm.q: The suspension of a motor vehicle is generally fitted on the front wheels but not on the rear ones.
1g7rlqm.why: Suspension is fitted on all wheels, both front and rear.

1stc9fw.q: The suspension of a motor vehicle serves to stiffen the vehicle so that the driver clearly feels every bounce caused by road irregularities.
1stc9fw.why: Suspension is there to absorb the bounces caused by road irregularities, not to pass them on to the driver.

1cszdku.q: The suspension of a motor vehicle does not come into operation on a straight road.
1cszdku.why: Suspension works all the time, even on a straight road, because no road is perfectly smooth and the load varies.

1axxeby.q: The suspension can become ineffective through wear or from having suffered very strong impacts.
1axxeby.why: Wear and violent impacts can damage the suspension and reduce its efficiency.

6ictd0.q: A vehicle with ineffective suspension has road-holding problems.
6ictd0.why: With ineffective suspension the wheels do not stay in good contact with the road, so road holding (tenuta di strada) gets worse.

148sxmj.q: Overloading the vehicle can lead to the suspension breaking.
148sxmj.why: A load above the permitted limit stresses the suspension too much and can break it.

vxhz9x.q: Overloading the vehicle can lead to temporary ineffectiveness of the suspension.
vxhz9x.why: When overloaded, the suspension is compressed to its limit and temporarily loses its ability to absorb shocks.

17355wf.q: Repeated overloading of the vehicle can lead to rapid wear of the suspension.
17355wf.why: Repeated overloading constantly stresses the suspension and speeds up its wear.

4swunz.q: A vehicle with ineffective suspension has reduced ride comfort.
4swunz.why: Ineffective suspension does not absorb road irregularities well, so ride comfort is reduced.

1mbuh5o.q: A vehicle with ineffective suspension increases the driver's fatigue.
1mbuh5o.why: With ineffective suspension the vehicle is less stable and less comfortable, so driving is more tiring.

1v34l7i.q: A vehicle with ineffective suspension can result in abnormal aiming of the dipped headlights.
1v34l7i.why: Ineffective suspension changes the vehicle's attitude and so the aim of the dipped headlights (anabbaglianti), which may dazzle other drivers.

4sfv26.q: Overloading the vehicle does not cause problems for the suspension.
4sfv26.why: Overloading puts excessive stress on the suspension, causing early wear and possibly breakage.

viddqw.q: If the vehicle is overloaded, to avoid suspension problems it is enough to increase the tyre pressure by one bar.
viddqw.why: Raising tyre pressure does not fix it: the load is still too heavy for the suspension. The maximum permitted load must be respected.

w3mrbj.q: The vehicle's suspension must be replaced roughly every thirty thousand kilometres.
w3mrbj.why: There is no fixed interval. Suspension is checked periodically and replaced only when worn or damaged.

1uws0ua.q: Overloading the vehicle makes driving harder, but does not cause problems for the suspension.
1uws0ua.why: Overloading makes driving harder and also stresses the suspension, which can wear out or break.

1yyea4n.q: The suspension of a motor vehicle, being made of elastic materials, does not suffer damage from impacts during driving.
1yyea4n.why: Even though partly elastic, the suspension wears and can be damaged by hard impacts, potholes or excessive loads.

1d1echp.q: The suspension of a motor vehicle is built so as not to need checks and maintenance for the whole duration of the vehicle's warranty.
1d1echp.why: Suspension wears and must be checked regularly, regardless of the warranty period.

1rka8lw.q: The suspension does not contribute to the vehicle's steerability, because this is ensured solely by the steering components.
1rka8lw.why: Suspension contributes to steerability because it keeps the wheels in contact with the road, which the steering needs in order to work.

2q8tss.q: Since cars have suspension on every wheel, the failure of just one of the four does not cause driving problems.
2q8tss.why: Even one broken suspension unit compromises stability, road holding and braking, so it is dangerous.

q0gvzv.q: The shock absorbers of a motor vehicle serve to reduce the oscillations of the suspension.
q0gvzv.why: Shock absorbers (ammortizzatori) damp the oscillations of the suspension springs, preventing repeated bouncing.

jpbcl1.q: Shock absorbers contribute to the vehicle's road holding.
jpbcl1.why: By damping oscillations, shock absorbers keep the wheels on the road and improve road holding.

1nxvpxs.q: Shock absorbers serve, among other things, to ensure the vehicle's road holding.
1nxvpxs.why: One function of shock absorbers is to ensure road holding by keeping the wheels in contact with the road.

14mk8jb.q: Overloading the vehicle can make the shock absorbers ineffective.
14mk8jb.why: Under overload the shock absorbers work beyond their limits and lose effectiveness.

1os4spf.q: Overloading the vehicle can cause early wear of the shock absorbers.
1os4spf.why: Overloading stresses the shock absorbers too much, so they wear out sooner than normal.

8bm8us.q: The shock absorbers of a motor vehicle do not need checks and maintenance for as long as the vehicle's warranty lasts.
8bm8us.why: Shock absorbers wear with use and must be checked regularly, regardless of the warranty.

1v4w9ok.q: Overloading does not cause problems for the shock absorbers of a motor vehicle if the driver adopts a careful driving style.
1v4w9ok.why: Overloading harms the shock absorbers whatever the driving style. It is the weight that matters, not how carefully you drive.

1fh0mut.q: If the vehicle is overloaded, to avoid problems for the shock absorbers it is enough to increase the tyre pressure by half a bar.
1fh0mut.why: Inflating the tyres more does not relieve the load on the shock absorbers. The maximum permitted load must be respected.

1nmt125.q: The driver can in any case adjust the stiffness of the shock absorbers.
1nmt125.why: Only some vehicles have adjustable shock absorbers. In general the driver cannot adjust their stiffness.

16niq00.q: The stiffness of the shock absorbers of a motor vehicle can be checked by the vehicle owner without going to a specialised workshop.
16niq00.why: Checking shock absorbers requires specific equipment and expertise, so it must be done in a specialised workshop.

xixczz.q: Worn-out shock absorbers cause abnormal behaviour of the vehicle when braking.
xixczz.why: Worn shock absorbers (ammortizzatori scarichi) reduce stability under braking and lengthen stopping distance.

5jni6f.q: Worn-out shock absorbers cause abnormal behaviour of the vehicle, particularly in bends.
5jni6f.why: With worn shock absorbers the vehicle sways and loses grip, especially in corners.

1usmdi1.q: In a motor vehicle, worn-out shock absorbers cause uneven wear of the tyre tread.
1usmdi1.why: Worn shock absorbers let the wheels bounce on the road, causing uneven tread wear.

vojde7.q: In a motor vehicle, worn-out shock absorbers increase the risk of the suspension springs breaking.
vojde7.why: Without the damping of the shock absorbers, the springs work harder and risk breaking.

10f3hod.q: In a motor vehicle, worn-out shock absorbers cause a decrease in the passengers' ride comfort.
10f3hod.why: Worn shock absorbers do not damp oscillations, so the vehicle bounces and passenger comfort drops.

1nlrpgr.q: In a motor vehicle, worn-out shock absorbers worsen road holding.
1nlrpgr.why: The wheels do not stay in contact with the road as they should, so road holding gets worse.

1jq1gpu.q: In a vehicle, worn-out shock absorbers cause abnormal engine operation.
1jq1gpu.why: Shock absorbers are part of the suspension and have no effect on how the engine runs.

a01yn1.q: In a motor vehicle, worn-out shock absorbers cause higher lubricant consumption.
a01yn1.why: Lubricant consumption depends on the engine. Worn shock absorbers do not affect it.

g663ri.q: In a motor vehicle, worn-out shock absorbers, by lowering the chassis height from the ground, improve the vehicle's road holding, especially in bends.
g663ri.why: Worn shock absorbers worsen road holding, especially in bends. A lower chassis does not make up for the lost grip.

12f50t7.q: In a motor vehicle, shock absorbers can be replaced with reinforced suspension.
12f50t7.why: Shock absorbers and suspension have different, complementary roles. Reinforced suspension cannot replace shock absorbers.

2gx052.q: A motor vehicle has suspension or shock absorbers, but rarely both.
2gx052.why: Vehicles have both suspension and shock absorbers, working together.

12pkcqn.q: The shock absorbers of a vehicle, if they are of the sealed type, require no maintenance.
12pkcqn.why: Even sealed shock absorbers (ammortizzatori) wear out, so they must be checked regularly and replaced when they lose efficiency.

1ehhhzm.q: If the power steering fails, the steering becomes "heavy".
1ehhhzm.why: Without power steering (servosterzo) assistance you need much more force on the wheel, so the steering feels heavy.

1gatbx0.q: If a tyre is punctured, the steering pulls towards the side of the punctured wheel.
1gatbx0.why: The flat wheel creates more rolling resistance, so the vehicle pulls towards the punctured side.

1k6vcmm.q: To ensure road safety, you must periodically check that there is no abnormal play in the steering.
1k6vcmm.why: Abnormal play in the steering makes control imprecise, so it must be checked regularly.

jplrac.q: Steering that feels "hard" may indicate insufficient tyre pressure.
jplrac.why: Under-inflated tyres increase the contact area and friction, making the steering harder to turn.

450pdm.q: Hydraulic power steering does not work when the engine is off.
450pdm.why: Hydraulic power steering uses a pump driven by the engine, so with the engine off there is no assistance and the steering is heavy.

scelvz.q: Excessive play in the steering makes the vehicle's trajectory imprecise.
scelvz.why: With excessive play, the movement of the steering wheel is not transmitted promptly to the wheels, so the trajectory becomes imprecise.

n8b07.q: Wheel toe (convergenza) affects the precision of steering.
n8b07.why: Toe alignment (convergenza) is the angle of the front wheels; if it is wrong, steering loses precision and tyres wear abnormally.

1ih2o7e.q: If the steering wheel vibrates, it is advisable to have the balancing of the front wheels checked.
1ih2o7e.why: Steering wheel vibration is usually caused by unbalanced front wheels, since those are the ones connected to the steering.

1chb3h5.q: Power steering helps to control the vehicle's trajectory in case of a tyre puncture.
1chb3h5.why: Power steering reduces the effort needed and helps counteract the vehicle's tendency to pull towards the punctured wheel.

4haap5.q: Power steering improves the vehicle's braking action.
4haap5.why: Power steering (servosterzo) only makes turning easier; braking depends on the brake system, not the steering.

t99dbj.q: If a tyre is punctured, the steering pulls in the direction opposite to the punctured wheel.
t99dbj.why: With a puncture the steering pulls towards the side of the punctured wheel, not the opposite one.

xte4ix.q: If the steering wheel vibrates, you must have the balancing of the rear wheels checked.
xte4ix.why: Steering wheel vibration comes from the front wheels, which are connected to the steering, so their balancing must be checked.

1wzgm33.q: A failure of the power steering shows up as excessive ease of steering.
1wzgm33.why: When power steering fails, the steering becomes heavy and hard to turn, not easier.

xmt3um.q: The steering wheel must be held in its lower part, with both hands below the spokes.
xmt3um.why: The steering wheel must be held with both hands on the rim in the upper half (about 9 and 3 o'clock), not below the spokes.

1qyli4.q: The steering wheel cannot be adjusted in height.
1qyli4.why: On many vehicles the steering wheel can be adjusted in height, and often in reach too, to get a correct driving position.

1ehpn98.q: The precision of steering is not affected by poor condition of the suspension and shock absorbers.
1ehpn98.why: Poor suspension and shock absorbers worsen road contact and therefore the precision of steering.

wxmkd6.q: The precision of steering is affected by low lubricating oil pressure.
wxmkd6.why: Engine oil pressure concerns engine lubrication, not the steering, so steering precision is not affected by it.

yq1oig.q: The precision of steering is affected by excessive coolant temperature.
yq1oig.why: Coolant temperature concerns the engine and does not affect steering precision.

1ocah04.q: A deteriorated exhaust silencer (marmitta) increases the noise pollution produced by motor vehicles.
1ocah04.why: A damaged or deteriorated silencer (marmitta) dampens engine noise less, so noise pollution increases.

1v2vx5n.q: A deteriorated silencer must be replaced with another of a type approved for that kind of vehicle.
1v2vx5n.why: The replacement must be type-approved for that vehicle so that noise and emissions stay within legal limits.

u6i4ee.q: The purpose of the exhaust system is to channel exhaust gases outside after reducing their toxicity.
u6i4ee.why: The exhaust system, thanks to the catalytic converter, reduces the toxicity of the gases before channelling them outside.

t3op4u.q: The purpose of the exhaust system is to channel exhaust gases outside after reducing their pressure.
t3op4u.why: The exhaust system, through the silencer, lowers the pressure of the gases before expelling them outside.

1gq5522.q: The purpose of the exhaust system is to channel exhaust gases outside after reducing their temperature.
1gq5522.why: Exhaust gases travel through the system and cool down before leaving the vehicle.

ajahfu.q: The purpose of the exhaust system is to reduce the noise of the vehicle.
ajahfu.why: The silencer in the exhaust system dampens the noise produced by the engine.

ylfweo.q: The purpose of the exhaust system is to reduce the air pollution caused by the vehicle's exhaust gases.
ylfweo.why: The catalytic converter in the exhaust system reduces the pollutants in the gases.

m7xcx8.q: The exhaust system must be completely replaced at every lubricant change.
m7xcx8.why: The exhaust system is not replaced at oil changes; it is only inspected and replaced when damaged or worn.

d00wlx.q: The exhaust system of electric vehicles needs more frequent maintenance than that of internal combustion vehicles.
d00wlx.why: Electric vehicles have no exhaust system, so they need no maintenance of this kind.

1k1wxze.q: Outside built-up areas, vehicles may travel without a silencer.
1k1wxze.why: A silencer is compulsory everywhere; driving without one is forbidden and penalised even outside built-up areas.

dv88gd.q: If the silencer's exhaust pipe gets a hole and you do not intend to replace it soon, you can repair it by wrapping it in glass wool and insulating tape.
dv88gd.why: A makeshift repair is not acceptable: the holed part must be replaced with an approved one, because noise and gas emissions exceed legal limits.

1vzfrv0.q: Replacing the exhaust pipe can also be done personally, without going to an authorised workshop.
1vzfrv0.why: The replacement should be done by an authorised workshop, which fits approved parts and ensures the system works properly.

k5nayg.q: It is possible to modify the exhaust system, provided you self-certify that this does not increase fuel consumption.
k5nayg.why: The exhaust system cannot be modified on the basis of a self-declaration: any change needs type approval and updated vehicle documents.

b5wdc5.q: Tampering with the exhaust system carries no penalty, as long as you only drive in urban areas.
b5wdc5.why: Tampering with the exhaust system is penalised everywhere, in towns and outside them alike.

1bb12gs.q: On two-wheeled motor vehicles, the engine can also be switched off using the emergency switch on the handlebar.
1bb12gs.why: The emergency switch on the handlebar lets you stop the engine immediately.

bviupj.q: On two-wheeled motor vehicles, to start the engine the emergency switch on the handlebar must be set to ON/Start.
bviupj.why: If the emergency switch is OFF the engine will not start, so it must be set to ON/Start.

kosccd.q: On two-wheeled motor vehicles, the emergency switch lets you switch off the engine without taking your hands off the handlebar.
kosccd.why: The switch is on the handlebar, within finger reach, so you can stop the engine without letting go of the grip.

x66xyw.q: On two-wheeled motor vehicles, the emergency switch lets you switch off the engine when stopped on steep slopes with your hands busy on the control levers.
x66xyw.why: On steep slopes your hands are busy on the brake and clutch levers; the switch lets you stop the engine without releasing them.

g69cmv.q: The emergency switch fitted to two-wheeled motor vehicles must be repaired as soon as possible if faulty.
g69cmv.why: It is a safety device, so if it is faulty it must be repaired as soon as possible.

owlk5f.q: On a motorcycle, to switch off the engine in ordinary situations it is preferable to use the ignition key rather than the emergency switch.
owlk5f.why: In normal use you switch off with the key, keeping the emergency switch for urgent situations.

1n8fmzm.q: On two-wheeled motor vehicles, the emergency switch on the handlebar replaces the key ignition device.
1n8fmzm.why: The emergency switch does not replace the key; ignition and locking of the vehicle remain handled by the key.

188ih4.q: To make switching off the engine easier, two-wheeled motor vehicles are fitted with an emergency switch located on the gear lever pedal.
188ih4.why: The emergency switch is located on the handlebar, not on the gear lever pedal.

lv0fhz.q: On two-wheeled motor vehicles, the emergency switch locks the wheels instantly.
lv0fhz.why: The emergency switch stops the engine; it does not lock the wheels.

1q94byb.q: The emergency switch located on the side stand serves to switch off the motorcycle's engine on sloping roads.
1q94byb.why: The emergency switch is on the handlebar, not on the side stand.

u3ay4g.q: To make switching off the engine easier, two-wheeled motor vehicles are fitted with an emergency switch operated by pressing with the right foot.
u3ay4g.why: The emergency switch is operated by hand on the handlebar, not with the foot.

1ct1uj9.q: On two-wheeled motor vehicles, the emergency switch works as a parking brake.
1ct1uj9.why: The emergency switch stops the engine and has no parking brake function.

w0sk76.q: On two-wheeled motor vehicles, the emergency switch is connected to the vehicle's anti-theft system.
w0sk76.why: The emergency switch only serves to stop the engine and is not connected to the anti-theft system.

64svgm.q: For road safety, on two-wheeled motor vehicles it is advisable to periodically check the wear of the drive chain.
64svgm.why: A worn chain can snap or jump off, so its wear should be checked regularly.

qrt8qy.q: The drive chain of two-wheeled motor vehicles, if not lubricated, may break.
qrt8qy.why: Without lubrication the chain wears faster and may break.

124unam.q: On two-wheeled motor vehicles, the drive chain connects the engine sprocket to the crown wheel of the wheel.
124unam.why: The chain transmits motion from the engine sprocket (pignone) to the rear wheel's crown sprocket (corona).

1plv5t0.q: For safety, on two-wheeled motor vehicles it is advisable to periodically check that the drive chain is well lubricated.
1plv5t0.why: The chain must be lubricated regularly to reduce wear and prevent breakage.

1t3dhvt.q: On two-wheeled motor vehicles, it is advisable to periodically check the correct tension of the drive chain.
1t3dhvt.why: A chain that is too slack or too tight wears out and may be damaged, so its tension must be checked.

jajkwf.q: On two-wheeled motor vehicles, a sudden break of the drive chain can lock the rear wheel, causing loss of control of the vehicle.
jajkwf.why: A broken chain can jam and lock the rear wheel, causing loss of control.

lznfig.q: On two-wheeled motor vehicles, if the drive chain shows signs of wear it must be replaced.
lznfig.why: A worn chain is dangerous and must be replaced.

1wgyjlp.q: On two-wheeled motor vehicles, the drive chain does not need lubrication because it is made of self-lubricating steel.
1wgyjlp.why: The chain is not self-lubricating; it needs regular lubrication to avoid wear.

yd8lkg.q: On two-wheeled motor vehicles, a break of the drive chain affects travel speed but not safety.
yd8lkg.why: A broken chain can lock the rear wheel and cause loss of control, so it does affect safety.

ihye69.q: On two-wheeled motor vehicles, if the drive chain shows signs of wear it must be reinforced with suitable iron wire.
ihye69.why: A worn chain must be replaced; it cannot be reinforced with makeshift repairs.

19v40jl.q: On two-wheeled motor vehicles, when replacing the drive chain due to wear, it is never necessary to also replace the engine sprocket and the wheel's crown wheel.
19v40jl.why: The sprockets wear together with the chain, so they are normally replaced along with it.

1qjhqh4.q: On two-wheeled motor vehicles, periodic checking of the drive chain tension is not necessary, because it has an automatic tensioner.
1qjhqh4.why: Chain tension must be checked periodically and adjusted when needed, even if the vehicle has a tensioner.

1i8ba3m.q: On two-wheeled motor vehicles, the drive chain must be cleaned with a degreasing detergent but absolutely not lubricated, so as not to make the gearbox slip.
1i8ba3m.why: The chain must be cleaned and then lubricated with a suitable product; lubrication does not make the gearbox slip, as the gearbox is separate from the chain.

wg1ovn.q: On two-wheeled motor vehicles, it is possible to replace the engine sprocket and the wheel's crown wheel so as to change the transmission ratio.
wg1ovn.why: The transmission ratio is an approved specification, so changing the sprockets alters it without authorisation.

bpjh5y.q: On two-wheeled motor vehicles, the oil level must be checked with the vehicle perfectly level, resting on its wheels and not on the stand.
bpjh5y.why: The oil level must be checked with the vehicle level and standing on its wheels, to get a correct reading.

ch0o43.q: On motorcycles it is necessary to periodically check the engine oil and brake fluid levels.
ch0o43.why: Engine oil and brake fluid are essential for safety and operation, so their levels must be checked regularly.

11olglg.q: On motorcycles, the brake fluid level is checked by looking at the dedicated transparent reservoir.
11olglg.why: The brake fluid level is read in its dedicated transparent reservoir (vaschetta).

7dnq1t.q: On some motorcycle engines, the engine oil level can be checked through a special small window on the engine sump.
7dnq1t.why: Some engines have a small inspection window (finestrella) on the sump that shows the oil level.

yi2n2l.q: On motorcycles, the lubricant level must be checked with the vehicle level and after the engine has been switched off for a few minutes.
yi2n2l.why: After shutdown the oil needs time to drain back into the sump, so check on level ground after a few minutes.

nlyn6s.q: On two-wheeled motor vehicles, there are no fluids whose levels need to be checked because the tanks are sealed.
nlyn6s.why: Two-wheelers also need checks of engine oil, brake fluid and, where fitted, coolant levels.

f345q2.q: On motorcycles, the engine oil level must be checked with the engine running at idle and the motorcycle on its stand.
f345q2.why: The level must be checked with the engine off for a few minutes and the vehicle level, not on the stand.

1wayj8u.q: Motorcycles are not fitted with a brake fluid reservoir because braking is purely mechanical.
1wayj8u.why: Motorcycles have hydraulic brakes with a brake fluid reservoir; braking is not purely mechanical.

1qmc5q0.q: On air-cooled motorcycles, the coolant level can be checked through a special small window between the engine fins.
1qmc5q0.why: Air-cooled engines have no coolant, so there is no coolant level to check.
